rules.title: Eastern daylight saving time 1918 (Standard Time Act, 1918)
rules.scope: Eastern zone (the 75th meridian): the cities covered here that kept its time

uncertainty.reason: The Act of 19 March 1918 advances each zone's standard time one hour from 02:00 on the last Sunday in March to 02:00 on the last Sunday in October. rules.title: New York: New York city time
rules.scope: New York, before standard time

end.note: The city resolved that its time conform to the new standard at noon on 18 November 1883; the Western Union time ball fell at noon Eastern time, and the City Hall clock was stopped at 12:12 city time (12:08:01.62 Eastern) until the new time caught up.

uncertainty.reason: The City Hall clock was stopped for "Three minutes 58 seconds and 38-100 seconds" to take up Eastern time, so city time was 4 h 56 min 1.62 s behind Greenwich (the longitude gives 4 h 56 min 1.4 s); that the city kept it from 1870 is assumed.

changes.summary: Flagged inferred: the report describes the city's time at the change of 1883 only, and the rule carries it back to 1870.

start.note: The city resolved that its time conform to the new standard at noon on 18 November 1883; the Western Union time ball fell at noon Eastern time, and the City Hall clock was stopped at 12:12 city time (12:08:01.62 Eastern) until the new time caught up.

uncertainty.reason: The mayor signed the resolution that from noon on 18 November 1883 all time in the city conform to the 75th-meridian standard.

rules.title: Baltimore: Baltimore city time

rules.title: Washington: Washington mean time
rules.scope: Washington, before standard time

end.note: Noon Eastern time on 18 November 1883, when the railroads and part of the city changed; the offset used here does not change.

uncertainty.reason: The Naval Observatory was to signal the new time "eight minutes and twelve seconds earlier" than Washington noon, so Washington time was 5 h 8 min 12 s behind Greenwich (the longitude gives 5 h 8 min 8.7 s); that the city kept it from 1870 is assumed.

changes.summary: Flagged inferred: the report describes the city's time at the change of 1883 only, and the rule carries it back to 1870.

rules.title: Washington: Washington mean time kept officially while standard time spread
rules.scope: Washington, 18 November 1883 to the act of 13 March 1884

start.note: Noon Eastern time on 18 November 1883, when the railroads and part of the city changed; the offset used here does not change.

end.note: The act took effect on its approval, 13 March 1884; when the departments and the fire bells changed is not recorded here, and the window runs to the end of March.

uncertainty.reason: From 18 November 1883 the railroads and the businesses dealing with them kept Eastern time, while other businesses, the government departments and the fire bells at noon kept Washington time until Congress acted; the atlas gives Washington time.

changes.summary: The window now ends at the end of 31 March, as its note says, not at the start of that day.

rules.title: Washington: Eastern standard time
rules.scope: Washington, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: The act took effect on its approval, 13 March 1884; when the departments and the fire bells changed is not recorded here, and the window runs to the end of March.

uncertainty.reason: The act of 13 March 1884 makes the mean time of the 75th meridian the legal standard of time in the District of Columbia.

changes.summary: The window now ends at the end of 31 March, as its note says, not at the start of that day.

rules.title: Providence: Providence time (local mean time)
rules.scope: Providence, before standard time

end.note: The city authorities adopted the new time on Tuesday 20 November 1883, two days after the railroads; the hour is not reported, and noon is used.

uncertainty.reason: The railroads centering in Providence were to make "a set back of 14 minutes and 40 seconds", so that "the railroad time will be fifteen minutes slower than Providence time". Taking the set-back as measured from Providence time, the atlas puts Providence time 4 h 45 min 20 s behind Greenwich (the report rounds it to fifteen minutes; the longitude gives 4 h 45 min 39.1 s) and assumes the city kept it from 1870.

changes.summary: City time now taken from the report ("a set back of 14 minutes and 40 seconds"), as for every city whose change a report measures, instead of from the longitude; reason corrected.

rules.title: Indianapolis: Indianapolis local time (local mean time)
rules.scope: Indianapolis, before standard time

end.note: Central time went into effect at noon on 18 November 1883, whether noon by the old time or by the new is not said, and the court-house clock was set back that afternoon; the jewelers were to change their regulators the next day. The window runs from noon by the old city time (11:44 Central) to 18:00.

uncertainty.reason: "Yesterday afternoon the court-house clock was set back sixteen minutes", so city time is taken as 5 h 44 min behind Greenwich, 16 minutes ahead of Central time (the report gives whole minutes; the longitude gives 5 h 44 min 37.9 s); that the city kept it from 1870 is assumed.

changes.summary: City time now taken from the report ("set back sixteen minutes"), as for every city whose change a report measures, instead of from the longitude; the reason no longer mentions fifteen minutes, which no cited source says.
The window of the change now opens at noon by the old city time (11:44 Central): the report does not say whether the change came at noon by the old time or the new.

rules.title: Louisville: Louisville city time
rules.scope: Louisville, before standard time

end.note: The fire bells rang noon by the new time on Sunday 18 November 1883, and the city clock was turned back 18 minutes, the report does not say at what hour. The atlas uses noon, new time; the window runs from noon by the old city time to the end of the day.

uncertainty.reason: A Paris, Ky., paper reports that "the city clock was turned back 18 minutes", which puts city time at -5:42:00; the mean time of the city's longitude, -5:43:02.3, is 62 s behind that, and the 18 minutes may describe the railroad's change rather than the city clock's. The atlas uses the report.

changes.summary: Flagged uncertain: the 18 minutes come from one second-hand sentence and differ from the longitude by 62 seconds; both readings are given. The adoption instant now has a window: the source does not say whether the change was at noon by the old time or the new, or when that day the clocks were set.

rules.note: The two readings differ by 62 seconds. tzdb's comments (a lead, not a source) say the Louisville & Nashville Railroad's trains were to stand still for 18 minutes at its change on 18 November 1883, which may be what the report's 18 minutes measures. The atlas takes the report's figure, as it does for every city whose change a report measures.

rules.title: Minneapolis: Minneapolis local time (local mean time)
rules.scope: Minneapolis, before standard time

end.note: Generally adopted on 25 November 1883; the hour is not reported, and noon is used, as in Saint Paul.

uncertainty.reason: No report gives Minneapolis's own figure, so the mean time of the city's longitude is used, 13 min 3.3 s behind Central time; neighbouring Saint Paul called its old time its "former meantime". That the city kept it from 1870 is assumed.

changes.summary: Reason corrected: Saint Paul's time now comes from a report, so Minneapolis, which no report measures, is no longer said to follow it.

rules.note: Offset computed from the city's longitude, 240 seconds per degree.

rules.title: Minneapolis: Central standard time
rules.scope: Minneapolis, from its adoption of standard time to the Standard Time Act of 1918

start.note: Generally adopted on 25 November 1883; the hour is not reported, and noon is used, as in Saint Paul.

uncertainty.reason: Standard time was to be "generally adopted in Minneapolis" on 25 November 1883, and two days later it was "working finely throughout Minneapolis", though "some are slow in adopting it"; action by the city government is not reported, and the public clocks are assumed to have followed.

changes.summary: Flagged inferred, as Chicago's adoption is: the reports describe general use, not the city government's action. A report of 27 November, after the change, is now cited (us-globe-1883-11-27-minneapolis).
